official_sources.title: STAC Item core identity, geometry, time and assets
official_sources.finding: A STAC Item is a GeoJSON Feature with required provider ID, geometry/bbox rules, UTC datetime semantics, links and an assets dictionary; API spatial intersection is based on geometry rather than bbox.
official_sources.limitation: Catalog metadata identifies candidate assets but does not prove that the linked bytes, CRS, epoch or elevation values are correct.

official_sources.title: STAC Asset href, media type, roles and overrides
official_sources.finding: Each asset has a required href; type and roles communicate media type and purpose, sidecar files should be linked, and asset-level properties can override Item defaults.
official_sources.limitation: Asset keys are non-semantic identifiers, so selection cannot rely on the key name alone and every override must be audited.

official_sources.title: STAC URI, media type and datetime best practices
official_sources.finding: Relative URLs require a precise self/base URI, trailing slashes are significant, media types should be specific, asset-level projection fields may override Item values, and time ranges should use explicit start/end datetimes.
official_sources.limitation: Best practices improve interoperability but are recommendations; the downloaded asset and its exact metadata still require independent validation.

official_sources.title: STAC Collection license, providers and extents
official_sources.finding: Collections require license and spatial/temporal extent, identify producer/processor/host provider roles, and require UTC RFC3339 temporal intervals; non-SPDX other licensing needs a linked license text.
official_sources.limitation: Collection extents are discovery bounds and cannot substitute for the exact Item footprint or raster-native coverage.

official_sources.title: STAC File Info size and multihash checksum
official_sources.finding: The stable File Info extension defines non-negative file:size and a multihash-form file:checksum on assets and links, plus byte-order and header-size metadata.
official_sources.limitation: A catalog checksum must be verified against the materialized blob; its presence alone is not proof and the algorithm encoded by the multihash must be accepted.

official_sources.title: STAC Projection asset CRS, shape and affine transform
official_sources.finding: The stable Projection extension defines asset CRS using proj:code/WKT2/PROJJSON, raster dimensions in Y-X order, and a six- or nine-element affine transform; asset-level fields override Item defaults.
official_sources.limitation: Catalog projection fields must match the opened raster exactly; shape ordering and GDAL versus Rasterio transform ordering can otherwise create plausible grid shifts.

official_sources.title: STAC Raster sampling, scale, offset and resolution
official_sources.finding: The Raster extension distinguishes area versus point sampling and defines bits per sample, spatial resolution, scale and post-scale offset; providers instruct users to apply supplied scale and offset.
official_sources.limitation: Raster extension metadata is descriptive and must be reconciled with the selected raster band, GDAL metadata and official product specification.

official_sources.title: Stable STAC API conformance and linked discovery endpoints
official_sources.finding: The stable STAC API exposes conformance, collections, per-collection items and cross-collection Item Search through typed link relations, returning STAC Item and ItemCollection objects aligned with OGC API Features.
official_sources.limitation: API conformance does not ensure complete provider inventory or immutable assets; the query, response, links and selected Item must be captured and reproducibly validated.
